name: Curved vs Straight Chairs & Tables: Liking at 84 ms and Unlimited Viewing
description: Faithful replication with the paper's own stimuli: Chuquichambi, Trawinski, Munar & Palumbo (2025), "Reassessing the curvature effect in tables and chairs", i-Perception 16(3) (Experiment 2, the online study). Participants rate how much they like the design of 80 greyscale furniture images: 20 chairs and 20 tables, each in a curvilinear and a matched rectilinear version (same style, material and use). There are two blocks of 80 trials in random order: in one, each object flashes for 84 ms and is replaced by a scrambled version of itself for 84 ms; in the other, the object stays until the participant responds and is then masked for 84 ms. Participants click a horizontal bar from 1 (dislike) to 100 (like); each trial starts with a 500-ms fixation cross. Ratings are stored per block (liking_brief, liking_full), keyed as category_pair_curved/straight, so curvature, category and presentation time can be modelled. Original result (50 Prolific participants): no preference for curved over straight chairs or tables at either presentation time; objects were liked slightly more at 84 ms (33.5 vs 30.7), mainly chairs; more novel and lighter objects were liked less. Images: the authors' stimulus set on OSF (osf.io/v69fx), edited greyscale product photographs originally collected from manufacturers' websites; used with the source named and removable on request. Differences from the original study: (1) runs in the browser instead of PsyToolkit, so 84 ms is approximate (about five frames at 60 Hz); (2) the six wardrobe practice trials are omitted because those images are not shared; (3) the scrambled mask is made by shuffling an 8 × 8 grid of tiles of the same image, the paper does not say how its scrambled versions were made; (4) image height is fitted to the screen instead of a fixed 13.8 cm.
author: Chuquichambi et al.
